ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, point $E$ is on side $AD$ and $AE=2ED$. $EC$ intersects the diagonal $BD$ at point $F$ and the area of $\triangle DEF$ is $2$. What is the area of $\triangle BCF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AE=2ED$, and $AD=AE+DE=3DE$,\\
thus $\frac{ED}{AD}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
Since quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram,\\
thus $AD\parallel BC$, and $BC=AD$,\\
thus $\triangle EDF\sim \triangle CBF$,\\
thus $\frac{ED}{BC}=\frac{EF}{CF}=\frac{ED}{AD}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
thus $\frac{{S}_{\triangle EDF}}{{S}_{\triangle BCF}}=\frac{ED^{2}}{BC^{2}}=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}=\frac{1}{9}$,\\
Since ${S}_{\triangle EDF}=2$,\\
thus ${S}_{\triangle BCF}=9\times 2=\boxed{18}$.

Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, AE=2ED, so AD=AE+ED=3ED, therefore ED/AD=1/3. Because ABCD is a parallelogram, BC=AD and BC∥AD; also because ED is a part of AD, ED∥BC.
